title: Pigeons en Ragoût d'Écrevisses (Pigeons with Crayfish Stew)
description: Prepared with pigeons, crayfish, and bouillon.

Pass them over the fire and add a pinch of flour, moisten with the cooking liquid from the pigeons that you pass through a sieve.
Let the stew boil for half an hour until little sauce remains.
Add a liaison of three egg yolks with cream, a little nutmeg, and a small pinch of very finely chopped parsley; thicken without boiling over a moderate fire while stirring constantly.

steps: Scald the pigeons, empty them, and truss the legs into the body; set the livers aside

title: Pigeons Gautier à l'aurore (Gautier Pigeons Aurora)

description: Prepared with pears, sugar, and water.
steps: Peel the pears from top to bottom, gather the stem slightly and cut off the small end.

When the sugar is melted, put the pears in to let them steep for two hours.
Remove them and dress them on wicker baskets, round end up, to pass the night in an oven of gentle heat.

Mix everything together
Add finely minced parsley, finely minced shallots, salt, coarse pepper
Grate a little nutmeg on top
Add three raw egg yolks

If you do not have a cooking utensil, put carrots, onions, a bunch of parsley and chives, two bay leaves, thyme, three cloves

title: Poitrine de Veau glacée (Glazed Veal Breast)

steps: Cut your breast as squarely as possible
Bone it to within two finger-widths of the tendons
Secure the meat with a trussing needle so that your breast is well rounded on top
Take care to cut the tender bones that extend beyond the tendons
Place your breast with the tendons facing down in your pan with a pot spoon of gelée
Cover your breast with lard bardes and buttered paper
Bring to a boil, then place over a gentle fire
Also place fire on the braising pan's lid
Two and a half hours of cooking are sufficient

If you do not have gelée to moisten your breast, add three or four carrots, four onions, two bay leaves, two cloves, a pot spoon of bouillon; if you have none, use water with salt, and a bouquet of parsley and chives
When your breast is three-quarters cooked, remove your vegetables and reduce your cooking liquid to a glaze
When your breast is cooked and the glaze is at the bottom of your pan, turn your breast so that the top side glazes
At the moment of serving, untie your breast and place it on your plat
Add two large spoonfuls of defatted grande espagnole sauce to your glaze with a spoonful of bouillon

title: Poularde à la Saint-Gara (Hen at the Saint-Gara)
